researchPageSubtitle: We combine physics-based control with machine learning to help robots operate safely, adapt to uncertainty, and work reliably beyond the lab. Our research connects sensing, learning, and decision-making across three application areas.

researchApplications.title: Intelligent Agriculture
researchApplications.tagline: Autonomy that adapts to the field.
researchApplications.description: Prairie fields change from one pass to the next. We develop robots that learn how the ground affects their motion and adjust their speed to balance accuracy, efficiency, and uncertainty.

projects.title: TerraGP-MPC
projects.subtitle: Learning the terrain while the robot drives
projects.description: A physics-structured Gaussian process learns how soil, crop stubble, and grass change the robot’s motion. Online model updates and predictive control help the robot track its path as it crosses unfamiliar terrain.
projects.imageAlt: TerraGP-MPC robot crossing tilled soil, crop stubble, and grass, with an illustration of online terrain adaptation.

projects.title: RA-SGP-MPC
projects.subtitle: Choosing speed from uncertainty
projects.description: How fast should a field robot drive? We use uncertainty in both the learned vehicle model and localisation to select its speed, slowing down where tracking is less reliable and gaining time where conditions allow.
projects.imageAlt: Drone views of risk-aware path tracking on wheat stubble and tilled soil, with the measured speed along a serpentine route.

highlight.title: Robotic sensing beneath the surface
highlight.description: We are also developing robot-towed ground-penetrating radar for soil-moisture mapping in Prairie agriculture, connecting autonomous navigation with soil science. Supported by UM’s UCRP and SREF programs.

mediaCoverage.title: Can AI teach a tractor to think?
Can AI help our agriculture sector?

researchApplications.title: Assistive Technology
researchApplications.description: We bring safe robot navigation together with rehabilitation research to explore useful assistance in everyday environments. Our focus is on user control, reliable motion, and the needs of people who use assistive technology.

projects.title: PRISM Shield
projects.subtitle: Safer navigation in tight spaces
projects.description: A safety filter uses live LiDAR point clouds and the robot’s actual footprint to check motion commands. It accounts for nonconvex shapes and operates in the robot’s body frame, reducing dependence on reliable global localisation.
projects.imageAlt: The lab’s Go2-W wheeled quadruped, a platform for footprint-aware navigation and safety research.

projects.title: Project BARK
projects.subtitle: Exploring assistive robotic K9s
projects.description: In collaboration with Dr. Jacquie Ripat and the Technology for Assisted Living lab, we explore how robotic dogs could support wheelchair users. The work centres on real needs, user autonomy, safety, and participation in everyday life.
projects.imageAlt: Jay Wang and Jacquie Ripat demonstrating a robotic dog with rehabilitation researchers at the Technology for Assisted Living lab.

mediaCoverage.title: Robot dog lends a helping paw

researchApplications.title: Arctic Exploration
researchApplications.tagline: Building autonomy for snow, ice, and remote environments.
researchApplications.description: Low traction and uncertain terrain make cold-region robotics especially challenging. We develop learning-based control and safety methods as foundations for future Arctic navigation and environmental sensing.

projects.title: Field Robotics on Snow and Ice
projects.subtitle: Learning to navigate on low-traction terrain
projects.description: Our uncertainty-aware learning-based predictive controller is evaluated in snow-and-ice field trials. This work investigates reliable path following under changing traction and builds a foundation for robots operating in cold and remote environments.
projects.imageAlt: Aerial view of the lab’s snow-and-ice robot field-testing area in Manitoba.
projects.imageCaption: Snow and ice field trials in Manitoba

highlight.title: Looking ahead: Arctic environmental sensing
highlight.description: Our longer-term direction connects mobile robot autonomy with environmental and subsurface sensing in collaboration with Arctic researchers. Ground-penetrating radar acquired through UM’s SREF program will also support this work.
